# Background/instructions
Determining which Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) on the West Coast of the US are best suited to developing marine aquaculture for several species of oysters and a species of your choice. Suitable locations will be determined based on range of suitable sea surface temperature (SST) and depth values for the species.

# Choose a species
- Red Abalone (https://www.sealifebase.ca/summary/Haliotis-rufescens.html)
- Depth: 0-24m
- Temperature:  8°C - 18°C

# Workflow outline
### Prepare data
```{r}
getwd()
# Load necessary packages
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(terra) 
library(tmap)
library(kableExtra)
library(spData)
library(spDataLarge)
library(geodata)
library(elevatr)
library(tigris)
library(here)
getwd()
# Read in the data
# SST files (rasters)
sst_2008 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2008.tif"))
sst_2009 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2009.tif"))
sst_2010 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2010.tif"))
sst_2011 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2011.tif"))
sst_2012 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2012.tif"))
# Depth file (raster)
depth <- terra::rast(here("data", "depth.tif"))
# EEZ file (shapefile)
wc_eez_sf <- read_sf(here("data", "wc_regions_clean.shp"))

# Combine SST rasters into a raster stack
sst_stack <- c(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012)

# Check the class of the new raster (sanity check)
class(sst_stack)
```

### Process data
```{r}
# Find mean SST
sst_mean <- mean(sst_stack, na.rm=TRUE)
sst_mean

# Convert avg SST from K to C
sst_mean_c <- sst_mean - 273.15

# Crop depth raster to match extent of SST raster
depth_crop <- crop(depth, sst_mean_c)

# Resample depth to match resolution of SST data using  bilinear method approach
depth_resampled <- resample(depth_crop, sst_mean_c, method = "bilinear")

# Check that depth and SST match in resolution, extent, and CRS
crs(depth_resampled) == crs(sst_mean_c)
# They do not match in CRS, so we need to match them
depth_proj <- project(depth_crop, sst_mean_c)
depth_resampled <- resample(depth_proj, sst_mean_c, method = "bilinear")
crs(depth_resampled) == crs(sst_mean_c)
# They now match in CRS.  Check resolution and extent
ext(depth_resampled) == ext(sst_mean_c)
res(depth_resampled) == res(sst_mean_c)
# They match!

# Let's visualize what we have so far:
prelim_sst_map <- tm_shape(sst_mean_c) +
     tm_raster(col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Mean Sea Surface Temperature (C)")) +
     tm_title(text = "Mean Sea Surface Temperature")
prelim_depth_map <- tm_shape(depth_resampled) +
     tm_raster(col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Depth/Elevation (m above sea level)")) +
     tm_title(text = "Depth")
tmap_arrange(prelim_sst_map, prelim_depth_map, nrow = 1) 
```

### Find suitable locations
```{r}
# Reclassify SST and depth data into locations that are suitable for oysters 
# Set as "1" if depth is between 0-70m, otherwise set as zero
depth_matrix <- matrix(c(- Inf, -70, 0,
                         -70, 0, 1,
                         0, Inf, 0),
                         ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
depth_reclassified <- classify(depth_resampled, rcl = depth_matrix, include.lowest = TRUE)

# Do the same thing for SST, setting to zero if temp is not 11-30C
sst_matrix <- matrix(c(-Inf, 11, 0,
                         11, 30, 1,
                         30, Inf, 0),
                         ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
sst_reclassified <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = sst_matrix, include.lowest = TRUE)

# Let's look at what we have now:
reclass_sst_map <- tm_shape(sst_reclassified) +
     tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(labels = c("Unsuitable", "Suitable")),
     col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Suitable (1) vs Unsuitable (0)")) +
     tm_title(text = "Mean SST Reclassified")
reclass_depth_map <- tm_shape(depth_reclassified) +
     tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(labels = c("Unsuitable", "Suitable")),
     col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Suitable (1) vs Unsuitable (0)")) +
     tm_title(text = "Depth Reclassified")
tmap_arrange(reclass_sst_map, reclass_depth_map, nrow = 1) 

# Find locations that satisfy both SST and depth conditions, using "lapp"
suitable_oyster <- lapp(c(sst_reclassified, depth_reclassified), fun = function(x, y) x*y)

# Map what we have now (the areas that satisfy the depth and temp requirements for oysters)
satisfy_map <- tm_shape(suitable_oyster) +
     tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(labels = c("Unsuitable", "Suitable"), values = c("grey40", "green")),
          col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Suitable Oyster Locations")) +
     tm_title(text = "Suitable Oyster Locations")
satisfy_map
```

### Determine the most suitable EEZs
```{r}
# Select suitable cells within West Coast EEZs.  We will need to overlay the suitability map and the EEZ map - this is a vector/raster interaction

# First, we need to make sure the CRS match
crs(wc_eez_sf) == crs(suitable_oyster)
# CRS do NOT match
wc_eez_sf_matched <- st_transform(wc_eez_sf, crs(suitable_oyster))
crs(wc_eez_sf_matched) == crs(suitable_oyster)

# Next, find area of grid cells
cell_area <- cellSize(suitable_oyster, unit = "km")
suitable_area <- cell_area * suitable_oyster

# Rasterize wc_eez_sf, so that both EEZ data and suitable sites data are rasters
wc_eez_sf_matched$id <- seq_len(nrow(wc_eez_sf_matched))
eez_raster <- rasterize(wc_eez_sf_matched, suitable_oyster, field = "id")

# Find the total suitable area within each EEZ
area_in_eez <- zonal(suitable_area, eez_raster, fun="sum", na.rm = TRUE)
names(area_in_eez) <- c("id", "suitable_area_km2")

# Create a final dataset of EEZs by area that is suitable for oysters
eez_fin <- wc_eez_sf_matched |> 
     mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
     left_join(area_in_eez, by = "id") |> 
     mutate(suitable_area_km2 = coalesce(suitable_area_km2, 0)) |> 
     arrange(desc(suitable_area_km2)) |> 
     mutate(rank = row_number())
eez_fin
```



# Function
Wrap all of the code inside a function so that it is reproducible for any species, provided that we know the depth and temperature requirements for that species.
```{r}
# This version of the function is further simplified so that the only input is the species of interest.  This relies on a pre-filled data frame for each species that contains the minimum and maximum depth and SST suitable for that species.  A version of the function that takes minimum and maximum depth and SST as arugments in addition to species is in the next code block.

# Create pre-filled oyster and red abalone dataframes first (can do this easily for any species of interest using data on SeaLifeBase)
oyster <- data.frame(
     name = "Oyster",
     min_sst = 11,
     max_sst = 30,
     min_depth = 0,
     max_depth = 70
)
red_abalone <- data.frame(
     name = "Red Abalone",
     min_sst = 8,
     max_sst = 18,
     min_depth = 0,
     max_depth = 24
)


# Now create the function, where the sole argument is the dataframe for species of interest
simplified_aquaculture_analysis <- function(species){
     # read in data
     sst_2008 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2008.tif"))
     sst_2009 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2009.tif"))
     sst_2010 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2010.tif"))
     sst_2011 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2011.tif"))
     sst_2012 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2012.tif"))
     # Depth file (raster)
     depth <- terra::rast(here("data", "depth.tif"))
     # EEZ file (shapefile)
     wc_eez_sf <- read_sf(here("data", "wc_regions_clean.shp"))
     
     # Clean/crop/reshape data
     sst_stack <- c(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012)
     sst_mean_c <- mean(sst_stack, na.rm=TRUE) - 273.15
     depth_crop <- crop(depth, sst_mean_c)
     depth_proj <- project(depth_crop, sst_mean_c)
     depth_resampled <- resample(depth_proj, sst_mean_c, method = "bilinear")

     # Filter for suitable locations
     depth_matrix <- matrix(c(- Inf, -(species$max_depth), 0,
                              -(species$max_depth), -(species$min_depth), 1,
                              -(species$min_depth), Inf, 0),
                              ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
     depth_reclassified <- classify(depth_resampled, rcl = depth_matrix, include.lowest = TRUE)
     sst_matrix <- matrix(c(-Inf, species$min_sst, 0,
                              species$min_sst, species$max_sst, 1,
                              species$max_sst, Inf, 0),
                              ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
     sst_reclassified <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = sst_matrix, include.lowest = TRUE)
     suitable_spots <- lapp(c(sst_reclassified, depth_reclassified), fun = function(x, y) x*y)

     # Calculate suitable area by EEZ     
     wc_eez_sf_matched <- st_transform(wc_eez_sf, crs(suitable_spots))
     crs(wc_eez_sf_matched) == crs(suitable_spots)
     cell_area <- cellSize(suitable_spots, unit = "km")
     suitable_area <- cell_area * suitable_spots
     wc_eez_sf_matched$id <- seq_len(nrow(wc_eez_sf_matched))
     eez_raster <- rasterize(wc_eez_sf_matched, suitable_spots, field = "id")
     area_in_eez <- zonal(suitable_area, eez_raster, fun="sum", na.rm = TRUE)
     names(area_in_eez) <- c("id", "suitable_area_km2")
     eez_fin <- wc_eez_sf_matched |> 
          mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
          left_join(area_in_eez, by = "id") |> 
          mutate(suitable_area_km2 = coalesce(suitable_area_km2, 0)) |> 
          arrange(desc(suitable_area_km2)) |> 
          mutate(rank = row_number())

     # Map suitability
     land <- ifel(depth_resampled > 0, 1, NA)
     suit_map <- tm_shape(eez_fin) +
          tm_graticules() +
          tm_polygons("suitable_area_km2", fill.scale =
               tm_scale_intervals(values = "viridis"), 
               fill.legend = tm_legend(
                    title = "Amount of Suitable Area\nin EEZ (km²)",
                    title.size = 0.6,
                    text.size = 0.5))  +
          tm_title(
               paste0("West Coast EEZs by Area Suitable\nfor ", species$name, " Cultivation"), 
               size = 1, 
               fontface = "bold") +
          tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom")) +
          tm_shape(land) +
               tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = "grey"),
            col.legend = tm_legend_hide()) +
          tm_layout(bg.color = "lightblue") +
          tm_options(component.autoscale = FALSE)
     suit_map
}

simplified_aquaculture_analysis(oyster)
simplified_aquaculture_analysis(red_abalone)
```

```{r}
# This version of the function takes minimum and maximum depth and SST as arugments in addition to species, as specified in the assignment.
aquaculture_analysis <- function(min_sst, max_sst, min_depth, max_depth, species){
     # Read in data
     sst_2008 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2008.tif"))
     sst_2009 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2009.tif"))
     sst_2010 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2010.tif"))
     sst_2011 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2011.tif"))
     sst_2012 <- terra::rast(here("data", "average_annual_sst_2012.tif"))
     # Depth file (raster)
     depth <- terra::rast(here("data", "depth.tif"))
     # EEZ file (shapefile)
     wc_eez_sf <- read_sf(here("data", "wc_regions_clean.shp"))
     
     # Clean/crop/reshape data
     sst_stack <- c(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012)
     sst_mean_c <- mean(sst_stack, na.rm=TRUE) - 273.15
     depth_crop <- crop(depth, sst_mean_c)
     depth_proj <- project(depth_crop, sst_mean_c)
     depth_resampled <- resample(depth_proj, sst_mean_c, method = "bilinear")

     # Filter for suitable locations
     depth_matrix <- matrix(c(- Inf, -(max_depth), 0,
                              -(max_depth), -(min_depth), 1,
                              -(min_depth), Inf, 0),
                              ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
     depth_reclassified <- classify(depth_resampled, rcl = depth_matrix, include.lowest = TRUE)
     sst_matrix <- matrix(c(-Inf, min_sst, 0,
                              min_sst, max_sst, 1,
                              max_sst, Inf, 0),
                              ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)
     sst_reclassified <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = sst_matrix, include.lowest = TRUE)
     suitable_spots <- lapp(c(sst_reclassified, depth_reclassified), fun = function(x, y) x*y)

     # Calculate suitable area by EEZ
     wc_eez_sf_matched <- st_transform(wc_eez_sf, crs(suitable_spots))
     crs(wc_eez_sf_matched) == crs(suitable_spots)
     cell_area <- cellSize(suitable_spots, unit = "km")
     suitable_area <- cell_area * suitable_spots
     wc_eez_sf_matched$id <- seq_len(nrow(wc_eez_sf_matched))
     eez_raster <- rasterize(wc_eez_sf_matched, suitable_spots, field = "id")
     area_in_eez <- zonal(suitable_area, eez_raster, fun="sum", na.rm = TRUE)
     names(area_in_eez) <- c("id", "suitable_area_km2")
     eez_fin <- wc_eez_sf_matched |> 
          mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
          left_join(area_in_eez, by = "id") |> 
          mutate(suitable_area_km2 = coalesce(suitable_area_km2, 0)) |> 
          arrange(desc(suitable_area_km2)) |> 
          mutate(rank = row_number())

     # Map suitability
     land <- ifel(depth_resampled > 0, 1, NA)
     suit_map <- tm_shape(eez_fin) +
          tm_graticules() +
          tm_polygons("suitable_area_km2", fill.scale =
               tm_scale_intervals(values = "viridis"), 
               fill.legend = tm_legend(
                    title = "Amount of Suitable Area\nin EEZ (km²)",
                    title.size = 0.6,
                    text.size = 0.5))  +
          tm_title(
               paste0("West Coast EEZs by Area Suitable\nfor ", species, " Cultivation"), 
               size = 1, 
               fontface = "bold") +
          tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_out("center", "bottom")) +
          tm_shape(land) +
               tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = "grey"),
            col.legend = tm_legend_hide()) +
          tm_layout(bg.color = "lightblue") +
          tm_options(component.autoscale = FALSE)
     suit_map
}

aquaculture_analysis(8, 18, 0, 24, "Oyster")

```
